title: CRLR/52/2023 of SURAJ PAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY HOME, DEHRADUN

paras.text:
SL.
No Date
Office Notes, reports,
orders or proceedings or
directions and Registrar's
order with Signatures
COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
CRLR No.52 of 2023
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. P.C. Petshali and Mr. Naveen
Singh, learned counsel for the
revisionist/applicant.
Mr. A.K. Sah, learned Deputy
Advocate General along with Ms. Mamta
Joshi, learned Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Yogesh Upadhyay, learned
counsel for respondent nos.2 and 3.
The registration of the present
criminal revision before this Court has
been as a consequence to the challenge
given to the order of 01.04.2022, as it
was passed by the Court of Additional
Sessions Judge/ Special Judge POCSO,
Udham Singh Nagar in Special Sessions
Trial No.17 of 2022, "State Vs. Surajpal",
whereby the Court has framed the
"charges", for trying the present applicant
for the offences under Sections 363, 366-
A, 376(3) of IPC and Section 5(j)/6 of
Protection of Children from Sexual Offence
(POCSO) Act.
While putting a challenge to the

order of charge as framed by the Sessions
Court, the parties to the proceedings have
filed a compounding application by
invoking the provisions contained under
Section 320 of Cr.P.C., seeking
composition of the offence on the ground,
that now the parties to the proceedings,
particularly the complaint/ respondent
no.2 herein has solemnized the marriage
with the revisionist on 20.10.2020 and, as
a consequence to which, a boy child has
born on 29.08.2021.
In order to settle the dispute the
parties were called upon to appear in
person. The parties are present in person
and they have been duly identified by
their respective counsels.
This Court has also interacted with
the complainant, who admits the fact, that
the averments which have been made by
her in her statement as recorded before
the Special Judge, POCSO, Udham Singh
Nagar on 30.05.2022, the same facts have
been narrated by her in paragraph no.2 of
the statement accepting the factum of
marriage and a boy child having been
born out of the said marriage. The same
fact has been reiterated by her during the
course of interaction made by this Court

with the complainant/ respondent no.2.
This Court has also interacted with
the present revisionist, who has submitted
that after the marriage having been
solemnized between them, the
complainant is residing with her in-laws
and both of them are happily discharging
their matrimonial obligations.
The order sheet reflects, that on
number of occasions the Government
Advocate was granted time to file
objections to the compounding application
but the same has not yet been filed.
In that eventuality, once the factum
of marriage is accepted by the parties
including their counsel who are
representing them and particularly
looking to the changed condition that a
boy child has born 29.08.2021, it would
be a situation which would be irretrievable
in case if the Sessions Trial is permitted to
be continued against the present
applicant for trying him for the offences,
which are otherwise not compoundable
under Section 320 of the Cr.P.C.
This Court is of the view, that this
case would be one of the fittest case where
owning to the subsequent developments
which are not irretrievable harnessing the

criminal ability to be faced by the
applicant for offences for which the
charges have been framed which is
impugned in the present revision would be
nothing but a proceedings in futility
particularly when the complainant admits
the factum of marriage and the other
aspects narrated by her in the
compounding application.
Owing to the aforesaid statement
and the fact as narrated in the
compounding application, this criminal
revision would stand allowed and, as a
consequence thereto, the order of framing
of charges which have been framed by the
Sessions Court on 01.04.2022 as well as
the proceedings of Special Sessions Trial
No.17 of 2022, "State Vs. Surajpal"
pending consideration before the Court of
Additional Sessions Judge/ Special Judge,
POCSO, Udham Singh Nagar, by way of
Special Sessions Trial No.17 of 2022,
"State Vs. Surajpal" would hereby stand
dropped.
But the dropping of the said
proceedings, owing to the composition of
the offence as discussed already above
would be subject to the condition, that the
revisionist has made a statement before

this Court and has undertaken that he
would be getting his marriage registered
within a period of one month from today.
In case if the marriage is not
registered within the aforesaid period the
dropping of the proceedings by virtue of
today's order would have no effect as
such.
